mysystem.title: My System
mysystem.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
mysystem.note: The founding text of positional chess: blockade, prophylaxis, overprotection, the pawn chain and play on open files and the 7th rank.

fischer60.title: My 60 Memorable Games
fischer60.author: Bobby Fischer
fischer60.note: Fischer's own annotated games. A masterclass in the Najdorf, the Ruy López and clear, concrete calculation.

kotov.title: Think Like a Grandmaster
kotov.author: Alexander Kotov
kotov.note: Introduced the 'tree of analysis' and candidate moves: the method for calculating without blundering.

silman.title: How to Reassess Your Chess (4th ed.)
silman.author: Jeremy Silman
silman.note: Teaches you to read a position through its imbalances: minor pieces, pawn structure, space, files, development and initiative.

dvoretsky.title: Dvoretsky's Endgame Manual
dvoretsky.author: Mark Dvoretsky
dvoretsky.note: The standard reference for theoretical endgames: key squares, Lucena, Philidor, Vančura and more.

capablanca.title: Chess Fundamentals
capablanca.author: José Raúl Capablanca
capablanca.note: The world champion's primer. He insisted on studying endgames first because they reveal what each piece can really do.

reti.title: Modern Ideas in Chess
reti.author: Richard Réti
reti.note: The manifesto of the hypermodern school: control the centre from a distance and attack it later.

watson.title: Secrets of Modern Chess Strategy
watson.author: John Watson
watson.note: Explains how modern grandmasters broke the classical 'rules' and why concrete play wins.

vukovic.title: The Art of Attack in Chess
vukovic.author: Vladimir Vuković
vukovic.note: The classic work on attacking the king: the Greek Gift (Bxh7+), mating patterns and the conditions an attack needs.

predecessors.title: My Great Predecessors
predecessors.author: Garry Kasparov
predecessors.note: A five-volume history of the world champions, with deep analysis of their most important games.

philidor.title: L'analyse des échecs
philidor.author: François-André Danican Philidor
philidor.note: 'Pawns are the soul of chess.' The first book to treat pawn structure as strategy. His 1777 edition analyses the rook ending that bears his name.

delavilla.title: 100 Endgames You Must Know
delavilla.author: Jesús de la Villa
delavilla.note: The practical minimum of endgame theory every tournament player should know by heart.

greco1620.title: Greco vs NN
greco1620.note: Gioachino Greco recorded model attacking games in the Giuoco Piano. Several of them are still traps that catch players today.

legal1750.title: Légal vs Saint Brie
legal1750.note: The origin of Légal's Mate. A 'pinned' knight moves, the queen is offered, and three minor pieces deliver mate.

immortal1851.title: Anderssen vs Kieseritzky, 'The Immortal Game'
immortal1851.note: A King's (Bishop's) Gambit in which Anderssen gave up both rooks, a bishop and his queen to mate with three minor pieces.

evergreen1852.title: Anderssen vs Dufresne, 'The Evergreen Game'
evergreen1852.note: An Evans Gambit that ends in one of the most celebrated combinations ever played.

opera1858.title: Morphy vs Duke Karl & Count Isouard, 'The Opera Game'
opera1858.note: The model of rapid development: every move gains time, and it ends with a pin and Rd8#.

reti1910.title: Réti vs Tartakower
reti1910.note: A Caro-Kann that ends 9.Qd8+!! Kxd8 10.Bg5++ Kc7 11.Bd8#: the most famous double-check mate.

capamarshall1918.title: Capablanca vs Marshall
capamarshall1918.note: Marshall unveiled his gambit (8...d5) in the Ruy López against Capablanca, who accepted, defended and won. The gambit was later proved sound.

torrelasker1925.title: Torre vs Em. Lasker
torrelasker1925.note: The most famous 'windmill': a rook gives a string of alternating discovered checks and harvests Black's pieces.

capatartakower1924.title: Capablanca vs Tartakower
capatartakower1924.note: A model rook endgame. Capablanca sacrificed pawns to activate his king and keep his rook on the 7th rank.

botvinnikcapa1938.title: Botvinnik vs Capablanca
botvinnikcapa1938.note: A Nimzo-Indian in which White's doubled c-pawns supported a mobile centre, decided by the combination 30.Ba3!!

spasskyfischer1960.title: Spassky vs Fischer
spasskyfischer1960.note: Spassky beat Fischer with the King's Gambit. Fischer responded with his article 'A Bust to the King's Gambit' (1961).

fischerspassky1972g6.title: Fischer vs Spassky, game 6
fischerspassky1972g6.note: Fischer, a lifelong 1.e4 player, opened 1.c4 and won a model Queen's Gambit Declined. Spassky joined the audience's applause.

kasparovanand1995.title: Kasparov vs Anand
kasparovanand1995.note: Kasparov revived the Evans Gambit at the top level and won in 25 moves.

kramnikkasparov2000.title: Kramnik vs Kasparov, World Championship match
kramnikkasparov2000.note: Kramnik's Berlin Defence ('the Berlin Wall') neutralised Kasparov's 1.e4, and Kasparov lost his title without winning a game.

reti1921.title: Réti's endgame study
reti1921.note: A king chasing two goals at once. It shows that a king's diagonal route to the queening square can be as short as a straight one.
